```plato

    //==
    // # The public trigonometric surface on `Angle`
    //
    // `Angle` (`quantities.types.plato`) stores radians, and the scalar
    // trigonometric kernel is declared over radians-as-`Number` in
    // `intrinsics.library.plato`. This library is the thin, portable layer between
    // them: every function here unwraps `Radians`, calls the scalar intrinsic, and
    // re-wraps where the result is angular.
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * Angular results are `Angle`, never raw `Number`
    //     (CONVENTIONS.md - angles). The inverse family (`Acos`, `Asin`, `Atan`,
    //     `Atan2`, ...) therefore returns `Angle`, delegating to the `*Radians`
    //     intrinsics that differ only in return type.
    //   * `SinCos` returns the pair in (Sin, Cos) order, matching `MathF.SinCos`
    //     and the host `AngleIntrinsics.SinCos`.
    //   * The arithmetic and ordering members restate, at `Angle`, what the generic
    //     `IQuantity` bodies give every quantity type; they exist because these exact
    //     signatures were host intrinsics.
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trigonometric_functions

    //==
    // # Construction

    // The angle of the given number of radians. The one cast into `Angle`;
    // other units go through the conversions below (`Turns`, `Degrees`, ...).
    Angle(x: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(x);

    //==
    // # Circular trigonometric functions

    // The cosine: the x coordinate of the unit-circle point at this angle.
    Cos(self: Angle): Number
        => self.Radians.Cos;

    // The sine: the y coordinate of the unit-circle point at this angle.
    Sin(self: Angle): Number
        => self.Radians.Sin;

    // The tangent: Sin / Cos. Undefined at odd multiples of a quarter turn.
    Tan(self: Angle): Number
        => self.Radians.Tan;

    // The sine and cosine together, in that order — the pair every rotation
    // matrix and circle sweep needs at once.
    SinCos(self: Angle): Tuple2<Number, Number>
        => (self.Sin, self.Cos);

    //==
    // # Hyperbolic functions
    //
    // The hyperbola analogues of the circular functions, taking the radians
    // payload as the hyperbolic argument.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperbolic_functions

    // The hyperbolic cosine.
    Cosh(self: Angle): Number
        => self.Radians.Cosh;

    // The hyperbolic sine.
    Sinh(self: Angle): Number
        => self.Radians.Sinh;

    // The hyperbolic tangent.
    Tanh(self: Angle): Number
        => self.Radians.Tanh;

    //==
    // # IArithmetic and ordering
    //
    // Radians in, radians out. Angle times angle and angle over angle are
    // deliberately absent: neither product is a well-defined angle.

    // The sum of two angles. Not normalized.
    Add(a: Angle, b: Angle): Angle
        => new Angle(a.Radians + b.Radians);

    // The difference of two angles. Not normalized.
    Subtract(a: Angle, b: Angle): Angle
        => new Angle(a.Radians - b.Radians);

    // The angle scaled by a unitless factor.
    Multiply(a: Angle, x: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(a.Radians * x);

    // The angle scaled by a unitless factor, with the factor on the left.
    Multiply(x: Number, a: Angle): Angle
        => new Angle(x * a.Radians);

    // The angle divided by a unitless factor.
    Divide(a: Angle, x: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(a.Radians / x);

    // The additive inverse: the same magnitude, the opposite sense of rotation.
    Negative(n: Angle): Angle
        => new Angle(-n.Radians);

    // Total order by radians. Raw, not periodic: two angles a full turn apart
    // compare as different (see `EquivalentAngle` for periodic equality).
    Compare(a: Angle, b: Angle): Integer
        => a.Radians.Compare(b.Radians);

    // A digest of the radians payload, consistent with equality.
    Hash(self: Angle): Integer
        => self.Radians.Hash;

    //==
    // # Inverse trigonometric functions
    //
    // The public, `Angle`-returning surface over the `*Radians` intrinsics.
    // Each is a partial function: the arc- family requires its argument to be
    // in the domain of the corresponding forward function (`Acos` and `Asin`
    // need [-1, 1]; `Acosh` needs >= 1; `Atanh` needs (-1, 1)).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inverse_trigonometric_functions

    // The angle whose cosine is `self`, in [0, pi]. Precondition: -1 <= self <= 1.
    Acos(self: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(self.AcosRadians);

    // The inverse hyperbolic cosine. Precondition: self >= 1.
    Acosh(self: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(self.AcoshRadians);

    // The angle whose sine is `self`, in [-pi/2, pi/2]. Precondition: -1 <= self <= 1.
    Asin(self: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(self.AsinRadians);

    // The inverse hyperbolic sine. Defined for every number.
    Asinh(self: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(self.AsinhRadians);

    // The angle whose tangent is `self`, in (-pi/2, pi/2).
    Atan(self: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(self.AtanRadians);

    // The angle of the point (x, self) from the positive x axis, in (-pi, pi];
    // quadrant-correct, unlike `Atan`. The receiver is the y coordinate.
    Atan2(self: Number, x: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(self.Atan2Radians(x));

    // The inverse hyperbolic tangent. Precondition: -1 < self < 1.
    Atanh(self: Number): Angle
        => new Angle(self.AtanhRadians);
}
```
